Ted Whitney was a voice actor who voiced Terenas Menethil in Warcraft III. He passed away shortly after finishing his work, and Earl Boen took up the mantle as Terenas' voice actor with the character's return in World of Warcraft: Wrath of the Lich King.

A tell, or whisper, is a private message sent from one player to another, often denoted by the color pink in the chat window. This does not bypass ignore functionality, which means that the character being ignored will see a reply stating as such. It is also impossible to whisper opposite faction players.

Tempest Keep is a former naaru fortress in the Netherstorm in Outland. This crystalline fortress is now ruled by Kael'thas Sunstrider, the lord of the blood elves, and dominated by scores of his brethren. The structure is divided into three wings - satellites of the gigantic structure - with the fourth wing, the Exodar, now in the world of Azeroth as the draenei capital. The three remaining wings are differentiated by the different color themes: Botanica (Light blue), Arcatraz (Red) and Mechanar (Light purple).

The Temple of Ahn'Qiraj (displayed as just Ahn'Qiraj) is a 40-man raid dungeon located in Ahn'Qiraj: The Fallen Kingdom. It was released with patch 1.9 during a massive server-dependent event called the Gates of Ahn'Qiraj.
A term for when you are getting too many chat messages (tells) from too many people to do anything but reply and you're getting too many to keep up with or getting confused and doing mistells.

==Loot-quest system== Temple of Ahn'Qiraj loot-quests require tokens which drop from bosses, combined with a certain level of faction with the Brood of Nozdormu. (Zul'Gurub and all post-Naxxramas tier sets use a similar system.) Players must collect five scarabs of two certain types (for a total of 10), two stone idols of a certain type, and a single Qiraji item. When a player has the appropriate collection for a particular item and a certain level of reputation with Brood of Nozdormu, he or she can turn them in for the item. *Note: Scarabs can be found in both raid sizes (20 and 40), and are used in both Cenarion Circle and Brood of Nozdormu loot quests. Tel'athion's Camp is a small camp in northwestern Bloodmyst Isle. It is little more than a tent lit by torches with a worktable and many barrels of tainted water. The water is the byproduct of research by the camp's demented owner and namesake: Tel'athion the Impure, and has been seeping into Bloodmyst's Water supply. Shaman were asked to purify the water supply and kill the mad researcher by Aqueous to answer the Call of Water (Exodar, 5).

Telaari Basin is a deep cleft located north of Telaar in southern central Nagrand. It is populated by earth elementals and the occasional Windroc. Telaari Fronds (used in the Horde Greatmother chain) can be found in this area.
The Tempest Rift is the part of the Twisting Nether that surrounds Tempest Keep on all sides. The dungeon's wings all float in the rift and are attached to each other with unseen bonds of force.

Telkar Doomhammer was the father of Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer, and one of the best warriors in the Blackrock clan. He wielded the mighty Doomhammer, considered by some to be a weapon of prophecy. Some years after Orgrim and his friend Durotan encountered the Prophet Velen, Telkar died and the weapon was passed onto his son. Doomhammer was passed to Orgrim with these words: "It is said that the last of the Doomhammer line will use it to bring first salvation and then doom to the orc people. Then it will pass into the hands of one who is not of the Blackrock clan, all will change again, and it will once again be used in the cause of justice." Orgrim would then wield it until the day he died —

After his minions are dealt with, Lord Godfrey commits suicide by jumping off the cliff onto the jagged rocks below the village, unwilling to live with a worgen for a king. Telo was an AddOn developer in WoW's earliest days through Wrath of the Lich King. Several features in their addons were incorporated into other Vanilla-era addon projects, and many ultimately inspired official features later added to the game. In particular, Telo inspired: * The self-cast key (defaulting to alt) for friendly spells in patch 2.0.1. * The addition of multiple action bars in patch 1.3.0. Telo's works were distributed through the now-defunct WoW forums, and later uploaded as some of the earliest projects on WoW Ace (id numbers near 3000).

Temples of the Damned are unholy places of varying purpose, but mostly related to Necromancy, first used by the Horde and then the Scourge. The Horde's were made of skeletons from the extinct giants of Draenor and were referred to in Orcish as Grombolar, meaning "bowels of the giant".

The Terms of Use Agreement is a legally binding agreement which has to be ratified before one is able to play World of Warcraft. Players must accept this agreement when they install the game or a patch. It governs your use of and conduct on the World of Warcraft servers. This is different from the "End-User License Agreement" (EULA) (aka "License Agreement"). You must agree to the EULA before installing or patching World of Warcraft.

The Terrace of Repose is located on the grounds just north of the Scarlet Monastery entrance. It is one of the very few places in northern Lordaeron where the Plague of Undeath has not reached, and the Scarlet Crusade have been able to grow green hedges and maintain a fountain with water that is fresh rather than stagnant like the rest of Tirisfal Glades.

The Temple of Telhamat is a draenei stronghold and religious site on the northwestern frontier of the Hellfire Peninsula. The draenei here are called the Omenai, a religious order led by Amaan the Wise. When Velen and the majority of the draenei race left for Azeroth, these draenei remained on Outland to reestablish a presence at their holy places. When the Watchers entered Outland in their pursuit of Illidan Stormrage, Maiev Shadowsong visited the Temple of Telhamat and asked the draenei about Akama.

Tentacle or tendril is a general class of creatures that generally appear as some sort of stalk or tentacle coming out of the ground with some unknown possibly larger segments below. They include subclasses called eye stalks.

Ter'lij was a subordinate of Zul'jin during the invasion of Quel'Thalas in the Second War. He was tasked to stalk Halduron Brightwing, but was caught in an ambush by a disguised Halduron and faced his demise in the confusion.
Terokkar Chokeberry Bushes could be found around the Bleeding Hollow Ruins in Terokkar Forest.

Many camps and villages can be seen with tents. The tauren, centaur, mogu, and the Zandalari trolls are known to use tents for their dwellings. In Warcraft III, many races used tents. The Temple of Wisdom is one of the many Titan temples of the Storm Peaks, located southwest of Ulduar's Halls of Stone. The columns of the Temple are entwined by strange twisted growths, possibly some kind of plant growth or the dead tentacles of a forgotten one, as they bear a resemblance to the tendrils of C'Thun. Presumably, Loken - the Old God-corrupted master of the "sons of iron" - was the Watcher (or Keeper) of the Temple of Wisdom, as he can be found seated within its throne during the confrontation with his brother Thorim in The Reckoning (Storm Peaks). Loken can be found the final boss in the Halls of Lightning.

Temple of Order is a temple located in the northern part of the Terrace of the Makers. Decorated with chains, shields, and weapons, it was the domain of Keeper Tyr, who was absent during Loken's rebellion. There is no clear sign of a struggle and there are no guardians present, leaving the question of exactly what happened seemingly unanswerable.

Temuejin, the Second Khan, was a khan of the Red Tribe of centaur. He commanded from Spearhold in Desolace. Some have said that he had so great a supply of arrows in his armory that his archers could volley for three days before exhausting their ammunition. Temuejin shares the title "Second Khan" with Gelk, the deceased founder of the Gelkis clan.

The Temple of Winter is a temple located within the southern part of the Terrace of the Makers in the Storm Peaks. The temple belongs to Keeper Hodir, father of the frost giants. The frost giants who once guarded the temple were killed by Loken's pet fire giants and Hodir himself was taken captive in Ulduar. Consequently, the cold weather patterns previously set at the temple vanished. Following the war against the Jailer, the brothers Bronzebeard reported that since Hodir was freed, the cold-weather patterns that encircle his temple have resumed.

The Temple of the Forgotten is a large room in Drak'Tharon Keep that houses the lich Novos the Summoner. File:Drak'Tharon Keep old loading screen.jpg|The Temple of the Forgotten depicted on Drak'Tharon Keep's old loading screen.
Ten Tabards is a collections achievement earned for collecting 10 unique tabards.
Terokkar Turkey Time is part of the meta-achievement for Pilgrim's Bounty.
Temporal Displacer is provided as an objective for A Matter of Time. Given by Chromie, the item is used by the adventurer to reveal Temporal Parasites in Andorhal.

Terrace of the Sun is an area inside Sunwell Plateau. It is the third outside subzone of the plateau and, like the Parhelion Plaza, is where a majority of its mobs species is found lurking. It is overrun by various Legion demons and the felblood elves. The Terrace is split into 2 parts, the infamous gauntlet after the Dead Scar, and the open balcony & spiraling ramp section after the Witch's Sanctum that leads to M'uru.

Tenecto is a Community MVP for the Latin American World of Warcraft since June 18th 2010 and he's normally encountered on the [http://forums.worldofwarcraft.com/ US Latin American Forums]. He is known to be part of the organization of huge world-wide Horde PvP events in his realm.

Temporal Illusion is a passive buff rewarded inside the Escape from Durnholde Keep, Opening the Dark Portal, Culling of Stratholme and Well of Eternity instances in the Caverns of Time. In the first three of these instances (all except Well of Eternity), it is applied to all characters who are not humans, dwarves, gnomes or worgen, turning them into a human, dwarf, or gnome at random. The Well of Eternity version of this buff makes all characters appear as night elves.

The Tenebrous Cavern is a massive cavern located in eastern Abyssal Depths. This cavern was used as a lair (according to the Horde storyline) by Ozumat until the Horde, using the Verne, forced the creature to leave. The Horde then proceeded to set up a large base camp inside. The cave entrance is right next to the Lightless Reaches that wraps around the Shimmering Expanse.
Tentacle Horror is an elite tentacle in Sira'kess Front, Abyssal Depths. The tentacles have ensnared and captured Wil'hai.
Tender Aru is the tauren stable master that can be found at Silver Tide Hollow in the Shimmering Expanse.
__NOTOC__ Teo Hammerstorm is a Wildhammer dwarf shaman trainer located in Anvilmar in Dun Morogh.
Terokkar Chokeberries were picked from Terokkar Chokeberry Bushes at the Bleeding Hollow Ruins in Terokkar Forest.

Teresa Spireleaf is a quest giver located at the Ruins of Nordressa in Azshara along with the Image of Archmage Xylem and Xylem's apprentices. She will occasionally walk over and talk to Quarla Whistlebreak.
__NOTOC__ Terborus is a rare gyreworm found at the Scoured Reach in northern Deepholm, just outside the cave.

The Termination of Service is a legally binding agreement which has to be ratified before one is able to play World of Warcraft. It only applies to European regions and is an extension of the Terms of Use Agreement.
Temporal Pauldrons can be found inside Murozond's Temporal Cache after defeating Murozond in End Time.

High atop the frigid northern peaks of the Kun-Lai Summit looms the Temple of the White Tiger (or Tiger Temple), an ancient training ground protected by an elite force of martial priests, along with the spirit of the White Tiger itself. Near the building holding Xuen himself is The Emperor's Burden - Part 6, providing a small bit of lore about Shaohao, the last emperor of Pandaria. Interacting with the shrine is one of the objectives of The Seven Burdens of Shaohao, a Pandaria exploration achievement. The Tiger Temple Tournament takes place on the temple's grounds.
__NOTOC__ Tentacles of Iso'rath are tentacles found erupting from the hard ground around the Ring of the Elements in the Twilight Highlands, as well as the Maw of Madness and within Iso'rath.
Tentacles of Markaru are occasionally spawned by the hydra Markaru in Eco-Dome Sutheron in the Netherstorm. They can hit you with a knockback effect.

The Temple of Five Dawns is a large temple found at the center of the Wandering Isle. After Huo is returned to the temple, Master Shang Xi sends his best students off to find the other spirits of the isle.
Ten Bitterrage is a pandaren found at the Elders' Path on the Wandering Isle.

The Terrace of Ten Thunders was a massive mogu fortress now in ruins in northeastern Jade Forest. It's here the mogu Spiritclaws, a sect of assassin-priests, have been calling forth ancient spirits to be used in the ancient mogu statues that litter the ruins. Shan Jitong, leader of these conjurers, has begun a large scale ritual to summon several spirits. While in the process the spirit of Pei-Zhi was called forth and aids the heroes in stopping this ritual. At the ruins' northwest end is the Seat of the Spirit Waker, while further west is Tideview Thicket.

The Temple of the Red Crane (or the Crane Temple) is the home of the August Celestial Chi-Ji, the celestial embodiment of hope, located in south-central Krasarang Wilds. From within the temple's ornate halls, the Red Crane wings out to oppose the despair that spread through the murky Krasarang Wilds like a cancer. The Sha of Despair and its minions have infested the area from the temple's basement, where Chi-Ji resides but was later cleansed by Prince Anduin Wrynn and heroic adventurers. With the recent arrival of Horde occupation forces, the sacred site has become a fortification and the Crane's servants hostages.
